paragraphs.text: And he went out from thence; and he cometh into his own country; and his disciples follow him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἐκεῖθεν, καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθοῦσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai exēlthen ekeithen, kai erchetai eis tēn patrida autou, kai akolouthousin autō hoi mathētai autou.

paragraphs.text: And when the sabbath was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, Whence hath this man these things? and, What is the wisdom that is given unto this man, and [what mean] such mighty works wrought by his hands?
paragraphs.original: καὶ γενομένου σαββάτου ἤρξατο διδάσκειν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ· καὶ οἱ πολλοὶ ἀκούοντες ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες· Πόθεν τούτῳ ταῦτα, καὶ τίς ἡ σοφία ἡ δοθεῖσα τούτῳ, καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις τοιαῦται διὰ τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ γινόμεναι;
paragraphs.translit: kai genomenou sabbatou ērxato didaskein en tē synagōgē· kai hoi polloi akouontes exeplēssonto legontes· Pothen toutō tauta, kai tis hē sophia hē dotheisa toutō, kai hai dynameis toiautai dia tōn cheirōn autou ginomenai;

paragraphs.text: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, and Joses, and Judas, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended in him.
paragraphs.original: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τέκτων, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς Μαρίας καὶ ἀδελφὸς Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσῆτος καὶ Ἰούδα καὶ Σίμωνος; καὶ οὐκ εἰσὶν αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ ὧδε πρὸς ἡμᾶς; καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ouch houtos estin ho tektōn, ho hyios tēs Marias kai adelphos Iakōbou kai Iōsētos kai Iouda kai Simōnos; kai ouk eisin hai adelphai autou hōde pros hēmas; kai eskandalizonto en autō.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honor, save in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τοῖς συγγενεῦσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois ho Iēsous hoti Ouk estin prophētēs atimos ei mē en tē patridi autou kai en tois syngeneusin autou kai en tē oikia autou.

paragraphs.text: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐδύνατο ἐκεῖ ποιῆσαι οὐδεμίαν δύναμιν, εἰ μὴ ὀλίγοις ἀρρώστοις ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας ἐθεράπευσεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk edynato ekei poiēsai oudemian dynamin, ei mē oligois arrōstois epitheis tas cheiras etherapeusen·

paragraphs.text: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages teaching.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐθαύμαζεν διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν. Καὶ περιῆγεν τὰς κώμας κύκλῳ διδάσκων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ethaumazen dia tēn apistian autōn. Kai periēgen tas kōmas kyklō didaskōn.

paragraphs.text: And he calleth unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits;
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκαλεῖται τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοὺς ἀποστέλλειν δύο δύο, καὶ ἐδίδου αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν ἀκαθάρτων,
paragraphs.translit: kai proskaleitai tous dōdeka, kai ērxato autous apostellein dyo dyo, kai edidou autois exousian tōn pneumatōn tōn akathartōn,

paragraphs.text: and he charged them that they should take nothing for [their] journey, save a staff only; no bread, no wallet, now money in their purse;
paragraphs.original: καὶ παρήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδὲν αἴρωσιν εἰς ὁδὸν εἰ μὴ ῥάβδον μόνον, μὴ ἄρτον, μὴ πήραν, μὴ εἰς τὴν ζώνην χαλκόν,
paragraphs.translit: kai parēngeilen autois hina mēden airōsin eis hodon ei mē rhabdon monon, mē arton, mē pēran, mē eis tēn zōnēn chalkon,

paragraphs.text: but [to go] shod with sandals: and, [said he], put not on two coats.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ὑποδεδεμένους σανδάλια, καὶ μὴ ἐνδύσησθε δύο χιτῶνας.
paragraphs.translit: alla hypodedemenous sandalia, kai mē endysēsthe dyo chitōnas.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Wheresoever ye enter into a house, there abide till ye depart thence.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου ἐὰν εἰσέλθητε εἰς οἰκίαν, ἐκεῖ μένετε ἕως ἂν ἐξέλθητε ἐκεῖθεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois· Hopou ean eiselthēte eis oikian, ekei menete heōs an exelthēte ekeithen.

paragraphs.text: And whatsoever place shall not receive you, and they hear you not, as ye go forth thence, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὃς ἂν τόπος μὴ δέξηται ὑμᾶς μηδὲ ἀκούσωσιν ὑμῶν, ἐκπορευόμενοι ἐκεῖθεν ἐκτινάξατε τὸν χοῦν τὸν ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν ὑμῶν εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai hos an topos mē dexētai hymas mēde akousōsin hymōn, ekporeuomenoi ekeithen ektinaxate ton choun ton hypokatō tōn podōn hymōn eis martyrion autois.

paragraphs.text: And they went out, and preached that [men] should repent.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν ἵνα μετανοῶσιν,
paragraphs.translit: Kai exelthontes ekēryxan hina metanoōsin,

paragraphs.text: And they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ δαιμόνια πολλὰ ἐξέβαλλον, καὶ ἤλειφον ἐλαίῳ πολλοὺς ἀρρώστους καὶ ἐθεράπευον.
paragraphs.translit: kai daimonia polla exeballon, kai ēleiphon elaiō pollous arrōstous kai etherapeuon.

paragraphs.text: And king Herod heard [thereof]; for his name had become known: and he said, John the Baptizer is risen from the dead, and therefore do these powers work in him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἤκουσεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἡρῴδης, φανερὸν γὰρ ἐγένετο τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐγήγερται ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐνεργοῦσιν αἱ δυνάμεις ἐν αὐτῷ·
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēkousen ho basileus Hērōdēs, phaneron gar egeneto to onoma autou, kai elegon hoti Iōannēs ho baptizōn egēgertai ek nekrōn, kai dia touto energousin hai dynameis en autō·

paragraphs.text: But others said, It is Elijah. And others said, [It is] a prophet, [even] as one of the prophets.
paragraphs.original: ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίας ἐστίν· ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον ὅτι προφήτης ὡς εἷς τῶν προφητῶν.
paragraphs.translit: alloi de elegon hoti Ēlias estin· alloi de elegon hoti prophētēs hōs heis tōn prophētōn.

paragraphs.text: But Herod, when he heard [thereof], said, John, whom I beheaded, he is risen.
paragraphs.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἔλεγεν· Ὃν ἐγὼ ἀπεκεφάλισα Ἰωάννην, οὗτος ἠγέρθη.
paragraphs.translit: akousas de ho Hērōdēs elegen· Hon egō apekephalisa Iōannēn, houtos ēgerthē.

paragraphs.text: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip`s wife; for he had married her.
paragraphs.original: Αὐτὸς γὰρ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἀποστείλας ἐκράτησεν τὸν Ἰωάννην καὶ ἔδησεν αὐτὸν ἐν φυλακῇ διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὴν ἐγάμησεν·
paragraphs.translit: Autos gar ho Hērōdēs aposteilas ekratēsen ton Iōannēn kai edēsen auton en phylakē dia Hērōdiada tēn gynaika Philippou tou adelphou autou, hoti autēn egamēsen·

paragraphs.text: For John said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother`s wife.
paragraphs.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅτι Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου.
paragraphs.translit: elegen gar ho Iōannēs tō Hērōdē hoti Ouk exestin soi echein tēn gynaika tou adelphou sou.

paragraphs.text: And Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him; and she could not;
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ Ἡρῳδιὰς ἐνεῖχεν αὐτῷ καὶ ἤθελεν αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο·
paragraphs.translit: hē de Hērōdias eneichen autō kai ēthelen auton apokteinai, kai ouk ēdynato·

paragraphs.text: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. And when he heard him, he was much perplexed; and he heard him gladly.
paragraphs.original: ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην, εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον, καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ἠπόρει, καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho gar Hērōdēs ephobeito ton Iōannēn, eidōs auton andra dikaion kai hagion, kai synetērei auton, kai akousas autou polla ēporei, kai hēdeōs autou ēkouen.

paragraphs.text: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, and the high captains, and the chief men of Galilee;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ γενομένης ἡμέρας εὐκαίρου ὅτε Ἡρῴδης τοῖς γενεσίοις αὐτοῦ δεῖπνον ἐποίησεν τοῖς μεγιστᾶσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς χιλιάρχοις καὶ τοῖς πρώτοις τῆς Γαλιλαίας,
paragraphs.translit: Kai genomenēs hēmeras eukairou hote Hērōdēs tois genesiois autou deipnon epoiēsen tois megistasin autou kai tois chiliarchois kai tois prōtois tēs Galilaias,

paragraphs.text: and when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and them that sat at meat with him; and the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης καὶ ἀρεσάσης τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις, εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῷ κορασίῳ· Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς, καὶ δώσω σοι·
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthousēs tēs thygatros autēs tēs Hērōdiados kai orchēsamenēs kai aresasēs tō Hērōdē kai tois synanakeimenois, eipen ho basileus tō korasiō· Aitēson me ho ean thelēs, kai dōsō soi·

paragraphs.text: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὤμοσεν αὐτῇ· Ὅ τι ἐάν με αἰτήσῃς δώσω σοι ἕως ἡμίσους τῆς βασιλείας μου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ōmosen autē· Ho ti ean me aitēsēs dōsō soi heōs hēmisous tēs basileias mou.

paragraphs.text: And she went out, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptizer.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσα εἶπεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς· Τί αἰτήσωμαι; ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτίζοντος.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthousa eipen tē mētri autēs· Ti aitēsōmai; hē de eipen· Tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou baptizontos.

paragraphs.text: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou forthwith give me on a platter the head of John the Baptist.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσελθοῦσα εὐθὺς μετὰ σπουδῆς πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα ᾐτήσατο λέγουσα· Θέλω ἵνα ἐξαυτῆς δῷς μοι ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthousa euthys meta spoudēs pros ton basilea ētēsato legousa· Thelō hina exautēs dōs moi epi pinaki tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou baptistou.

paragraphs.text: And the king was exceeding sorry; but for the sake of his oaths, and of them that sat at meat, he would not reject her.
paragraphs.original: καὶ περίλυπος γενόμενος ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς ἀνακειμένους οὐκ ἠθέλησεν ἀθετῆσαι αὐτήν·
paragraphs.translit: kai perilypos genomenos ho basileus dia tous horkous kai tous anakeimenous ouk ēthelēsen athetēsai autēn·

paragraphs.text: And straightway the king sent forth a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring his head: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀποστείλας ὁ βασιλεὺς σπεκουλάτορα ἐπέταξεν ἐνέγκαι τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ. καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπεκεφάλισεν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys aposteilas ho basileus spekoulatora epetaxen enenkai tēn kephalēn autou. kai apelthōn apekephalisen auton en tē phylakē

paragraphs.text: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the damsel; and the damsel gave it to her mother.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤνεγκεν τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῷ κορασίῳ, καὶ τὸ κοράσιον ἔδωκεν αὐτὴν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēnenken tēn kephalēn autou epi pinaki kai edōken autēn tō korasiō, kai to korasion edōken autēn tē mētri autēs.

paragraphs.text: And when his disciples heard [thereof], they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousantes hoi mathētai autou ēlthon kai ēran to ptōma autou kai ethēkan auto en mnēmeiō.

paragraphs.text: And the apostles gather themselves together unto Jesus; and they told him all things, whatsoever they had done, and whatsoever they had taught.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ συνάγονται οἱ ἀπόστολοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν αὐτῷ πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησαν καὶ ὅσα ἐδίδαξαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai synagontai hoi apostoloi pros ton Iēsoun, kai apēngeilan autō panta hosa epoiēsan kai hosa edidaxan.

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while. For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Δεῦτε ὑμεῖς αὐτοὶ κατʼ ἰδίαν εἰς ἔρημον τόπον καὶ ἀναπαύσασθε ὀλίγον. ἦσαν γὰρ οἱ ἐρχόμενοι καὶ οἱ ὑπάγοντες πολλοί, καὶ οὐδὲ φαγεῖν εὐκαίρουν.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Deute hymeis autoi katʼ idian eis erēmon topon kai anapausasthe oligon. ēsan gar hoi erchomenoi kai hoi hypagontes polloi, kai oude phagein eukairoun.

paragraphs.text: And they went away in the boat to a desert place apart.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀπῆλθον ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατʼ ἰδίαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēlthon en tō ploiō eis erēmon topon katʼ idian.

paragraphs.text: And [the people] saw them going, and many knew [them], and they ran together there on foot from all the cities, and outwent them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶδον αὐτοὺς ὑπάγοντας καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν πολλοί, καὶ πεζῇ ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν πόλεων συνέδραμον ἐκεῖ καὶ προῆλθον αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon autous hypagontas kai epegnōsan polloi, kai pezē apo pasōn tōn poleōn synedramon ekei kai proēlthon autous.

paragraphs.text: And he came forth and saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον, καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ὅτι ἦσαν ὡς πρόβατα μὴ ἔχοντα ποιμένα, καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς πολλά.
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthōn eiden polyn ochlon, kai esplanchnisthē epʼ autous hoti ēsan hōs probata mē echonta poimena, kai ērxato didaskein autous polla.

paragraphs.text: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, The place is desert, and the day is now far spent;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἤδη ὥρας πολλῆς γενομένης προσελθόντες αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος, καὶ ἤδη ὥρα πολλή·
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēdē hōras pollēs genomenēs proselthontes autō hoi mathētai autou elegon hoti Erēmos estin ho topos, kai ēdē hōra pollē·

paragraphs.text: send them away, that they may go into the country and villages round about, and buy themselves somewhat to eat.
paragraphs.original: ἀπόλυσον αὐτούς, ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τοὺς κύκλῳ ἀγροὺς καὶ κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς τί φάγωσιν.
paragraphs.translit: apolyson autous, hina apelthontes eis tous kyklō agrous kai kōmas agorasōsin heautois ti phagōsin.

paragraphs.text: But he answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred shillings` worth of bread, and give them to eat?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν. καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἀπελθόντες ἀγοράσωμεν δηναρίων διακοσίων ἄρτους καὶ δώσομεν αὐτοῖς φαγεῖν;
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen autois· Dote autois hymeis phagein. kai legousin autō· Apelthontes agorasōmen dēnariōn diakosiōn artous kai dōsomen autois phagein;

paragraphs.text: And he saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go [and] see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους; ὑπάγετε ἴδετε. καὶ γνόντες λέγουσιν· Πέντε, καὶ δύο ἰχθύας.
paragraphs.translit: ho de legei autois· Posous echete artous; hypagete idete. kai gnontes legousin· Pente, kai dyo ichthyas.

paragraphs.text: And he commanded them that all should sit down by companies upon the green grass.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπέταξεν αὐτοῖς ἀνακλῖναι πάντας συμπόσια συμπόσια ἐπὶ τῷ χλωρῷ χόρτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai epetaxen autois anaklinai pantas symposia symposia epi tō chlōrō chortō.

paragraphs.text: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνέπεσαν πρασιαὶ πρασιαὶ κατὰ ἑκατὸν καὶ κατὰ πεντήκοντα.
paragraphs.translit: kai anepesan prasiai prasiai kata hekaton kai kata pentēkonta.

paragraphs.text: And he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake the loaves; and he gave to the disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κατέκλασεν τοὺς ἄρτους καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα παρατιθῶσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἐμέρισεν πᾶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai labōn tous pente artous kai tous dyo ichthyas anablepsas eis ton ouranon eulogēsen kai kateklasen tous artous kai edidou tois mathētais autou hina paratithōsin autois, kai tous dyo ichthyas emerisen pasin.

paragraphs.text: And they all ate, and were filled.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ephagon pantes kai echortasthēsan·

paragraphs.text: And they took up broken pieces, twelve basketfuls, and also of the fishes.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦραν κλάσματα δώδεκα κοφίνων πληρώματα καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἰχθύων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēran klasmata dōdeka kophinōn plērōmata kai apo tōn ichthyōn.

paragraphs.text: And they that ate the loaves were five thousand men.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦσαν οἱ φαγόντες τοὺς ἄρτους πεντακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēsan hoi phagontes tous artous pentakischilioi andres.

paragraphs.text: And straightway he constrained his disciples to enter into the boat, and to go before [him] unto the other side to Bethsaida, while he himself sendeth the multitude away.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν εἰς τὸ πέραν πρὸς Βηθσαϊδάν, ἕως αὐτὸς ἀπολύει τὸν ὄχλον.
paragraphs.translit: Kai euthys ēnankasen tous mathētas autou embēnai eis to ploion kai proagein eis to peran pros Bēthsaidan, heōs autos apolyei ton ochlon.

paragraphs.text: And after he had taken leave of them, he departed into the mountain to pray.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai apotaxamenos autois apēlthen eis to oros proseuxasthai.

paragraphs.text: And when even was come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὀψίας γενομένης ἦν τὸ πλοῖον ἐν μέσῳ τῆς θαλάσσης, καὶ αὐτὸς μόνος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai opsias genomenēs ēn to ploion en mesō tēs thalassēs, kai autos monos epi tēs gēs.

paragraphs.text: And seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary unto them, about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking on the sea; and he would have passed by them:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτοὺς βασανιζομένους ἐν τῷ ἐλαύνειν, ἦν γὰρ ὁ ἄνεμος ἐναντίος αὐτοῖς, περὶ τετάρτην φυλακὴν τῆς νυκτὸς ἔρχεται πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης· καὶ ἤθελεν παρελθεῖν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn autous basanizomenous en tō elaunein, ēn gar ho anemos enantios autois, peri tetartēn phylakēn tēs nyktos erchetai pros autous peripatōn epi tēs thalassēs· kai ēthelen parelthein autous.

paragraphs.text: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἔδοξαν ὅτι φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀνέκραξαν,
paragraphs.translit: hoi de idontes auton epi tēs thalassēs peripatounta edoxan hoti phantasma estin kai anekraxan,

paragraphs.text: for they all saw him, and were troubled. But he straightway spake with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.
paragraphs.original: πάντες γὰρ αὐτὸν εἶδον καὶ ἐταράχθησαν. ὁ δὲ εὐθὺς ἐλάλησεν μετʼ αὐτῶν, καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Θαρσεῖτε, ἐγώ εἰμι, μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
paragraphs.translit: pantes gar auton eidon kai etarachthēsan. ho de euthys elalēsen metʼ autōn, kai legei autois· Tharseite, egō eimi, mē phobeisthe.

paragraphs.text: And he went up unto them into the boat; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀνέβη πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος. καὶ λίαν ἐκ περισσοῦ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἐξίσταντο,
paragraphs.translit: kai anebē pros autous eis to ploion, kai ekopasen ho anemos. kai lian ek perissou en heautois existanto,

paragraphs.text: for they understood not concerning the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
paragraphs.original: οὐ γὰρ συνῆκαν ἐπὶ τοῖς ἄρτοις, ἀλλʼ ἦν αὐτῶν ἡ καρδία πεπωρωμένη.
paragraphs.translit: ou gar synēkan epi tois artois, allʼ ēn autōn hē kardia pepōrōmenē.

paragraphs.text: And when they had crossed over, they came to the land unto Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἦλθον εἰς Γεννησαρὲτ καὶ προσωρμίσθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai diaperasantes epi tēn gēn ēlthon eis Gennēsaret kai prosōrmisthēsan.

paragraphs.text: And when they were come out of the boat, straightway [the people] knew him,
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου εὐθὺς ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν
paragraphs.translit: kai exelthontōn autōn ek tou ploiou euthys epignontes auton

paragraphs.text: and ran round about that whole region, and began to carry about on their beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.
paragraphs.original: περιέδραμον ὅλην τὴν χώραν ἐκείνην καὶ ἤρξαντο ἐπὶ τοῖς κραβάττοις τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας περιφέρειν ὅπου ἤκουον ὅτι ἐστίν.
paragraphs.translit: periedramon holēn tēn chōran ekeinēn kai ērxanto epi tois krabattois tous kakōs echontas peripherein hopou ēkouon hoti estin.

paragraphs.text: And wheresoever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅπου ἂν εἰσεπορεύετο εἰς κώμας ἢ εἰς πόλεις ἢ εἰς ἀγροὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς ἐτίθεσαν τοὺς ἀσθενοῦντας, καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα κἂν τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν ἥψαντο αὐτοῦ ἐσῴζοντο.
paragraphs.translit: kai hopou an eiseporeueto eis kōmas ē eis poleis ē eis agrous en tais agorais etithesan tous asthenountas, kai parekaloun auton hina kan tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou hapsōntai· kai hosoi an hēpsanto autou esōzonto.
